channel.title: Lampasas Dispatch Record - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Lampasas Dispatch Record (lampasasdispatchrecord.com)

item.title: Local political party chairs reflect on primary election, runoff race to come
item.description: The 2026 November midterm election may be months away, but local political party leaders are still soaking in the results from the March primaries held two weeks ago. Lampasas County Republican Party Chair Wendy Daugherty and Lampasas County Democratic Party Chair Cyndy Burleson provided their thoughts on the primary season that saw Democrats statewide outnumber Republicans at the ballot box for the first time in over 20 years during a non-presidential election year.

item.title: Badgers rout Taylor for five-inning victory
item.description: Last Friday, the Badger baseball team finished off the series sweep of Taylor with their second run-rule victory in two district games against the Ducks. Lampasas won 16-0 over the Ducks in what was the district home opener.

item.title: Softball moves to 3-1 in district with win over Taylor
item.description: A four-run first inning was the difference maker for the Lady Badger softball team in its 6-3 win over the Lady Ducks last Friday. Two of the runs in the first inning were driven in by Madison Magilke and Emory Vineyard, while the other two scored on an error by Taylor.

item.title: Honing their welding craft
item.description: Valentin Renteria works with Lampasas High School welding instructor Stephen Byrd at Oldham Welding during spring break to refine her techniques. She and student Devon Lively are among those who have qualified for the state competition May 7-8.

item.title: Commissioners give updates on planned paving projects
item.description: As cooler temperatures wane and warmer temperatures arise, Lampasas County commissioners are set to begin precinct paving projects. Precinct 2 Commissioner Jamie Smart and Precinct 3 Shad Hill shared their plans with the Dispatch Record on possible upgrades residents may expect.

item.title: LISD holds first town hall on $139.6 million bond

item.title: Carroll, Rainwater outline upcoming road projects
item.description: Lampasas County Commissioners Bobby Carroll and Mark Rainwater are gearing up for road improvement projects now that temperatures are getting warmer. One priority for both commissioners is addressing maintenance on County Road 3300, which lies in both Carroll’s Precinct 1 and Rainwater’s Precinct 4.

item.title: EDC approves marketing package
item.description: The Lampasas Economic Development Corp. Board of Directors approved a $30,000 contract with Chase Kuker and Jordan Kuker for a multi-media package during Wednesday’s regular meeting.

item.title: Badger soccer loses 2-1 heartbreaker in bi-district round
item.description: An extra-time goal was the difference in the 2-1 boys’ soccer defeat in the bi-district playoff match last Thursday against Life Waxahachie. The Badgers played a very tough, defensive match through the first half and well into the second half before they finally found the breakthrough via a free kick that was put into the box by Parker Boykin.

item.title: City Council discusses water supply, Hostess House event bookings
item.description: On Monday, the Lampasas City Council heard a lengthy presentation on water from Jones-Heroy and Associates. Jason Jones outlined a water study that was many months in the making.

item.title: County residents voice displeasure over potential data centers in area
item.description: The Lampasas County Commissioners Court has committed to drafting a resolution opposing data centers and renewable energy projects like battery energy storage systems (BESS) in the county. The decision came after residents expressed concerns in Monday’s regular meeting.

item.title: Errors cost softball team in loss to Burnet
item.description: On Tuesday night, the Lady Badger softball team had trouble with errors and lost 10-5 to Burnet. Lampasas jumped out to a lead in the second inning with a two-run homer by Laynee Bretey.

item.title: Architect unveils bold vision for downtown area along creek
item.description: Stuart Alderman, an Austin-area architect, provided a glimpse of how the Lampasas downtown district could blossom by utilizing mixed-use zoning. Alderman’s remarks came at Friday’s Forward Lampasas meeting at First Texas Bank.

item.title: LCAD chief appraiser explains ag exemptions
item.description: Lampasas Central Appraisal District Chief Appraiser Juan Saucedo detailed how the district appraises agricultural land in a presentation to the Lampasas County Commissioners Court on March 23. Also, Saucedo touched on how local taxing entities will be affected by House Bill 9 that raises the exempted amount of personal business property from $2,500 to $125,0000.

item.title: Badgers cage Bulldogs on walk-off hit by pitch
item.description: As Burnet and Lampasas were tied 2-2 in the bottom of the seventh inning last Friday night, the Badgers came to the plate. After a couple of walks and a Cory White single through the left side of the infield, the bases were loaded for Tripp Stinnett who came off the bench to pinch hit for Jonathan Bowling.
